solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run found in woven tussore garment

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it, so one piece goes into the other
woven threads are interlaced, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A ladder discovered in a piece of clothing made of tussore silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges TUSSORE into TOUSERS, and 'found in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are an item of clothing worn on the legs, an example of a garment.

clue.text: Claw used in some brutal onslaught

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claw used in a savage attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Claw used' takes in the link 'used in'; the definition is just 'Claw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: A family saying arising with northern Turkish

indicators.note: arising in a down answer means rising up, so the words are read bottom to top

parts.note: a family motto is a saying on a coat of arms

explanation.surface: A household proverb coming from the north of Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottoman describes the Turkish empire and its people, so it can mean Turkish.

clue.text: Do peers meet to get involved in gauge for HS2?

indicators.note: letters that get involved become tangled together, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Should members of the House of Lords meet to join in on the HS2 rail project?
explanation.walkthrough: HS2 is Britain's planned High Speed 2 railway, hence a gauge measuring speed; 'gauge' looks like rail gauge but is a dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedometer is the instrument measuring how fast a vehicle travels, apt for a high-speed train.

clue.text: Rebroadcast programme about natural fuel

parts.note: re means about or concerning
peat is dug from bogs and burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: A television show being shown again about a fuel source.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat is a show aired again after its first transmission.

clue.text: Second favourite reversed dance movement

indicators.note: reversed says the word for favourite is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A dancer's second-favourite move, performed backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pattern of foot movement within a dance.

clue.text: One who inherits after time what's belonging to them

indicators.note: in this clue one piece after another follows it in the answer

parts.note: an heir is a person who inherits

explanation.surface: Someone who inherits, in time, what belonged to others.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive word for property owned by a group of people is this pronoun.

clue.text: Get rotten referee in place years

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A bad referee is installed somewhere for years.
explanation.definitionFit: To putrefy is to decay or decompose, so to go rotten.

clue.text: Able to remember role of landlord? Exactly right!

parts.note: a landlord lets property, so is cryptically one who lets
something exactly right is perfect

explanation.surface: An actor playing a landlord is word-for-word on their lines, and someone exclaims approval.
explanation.walkthrough: LETTER is a crossword joke: not a written message but one who lets out rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is word-perfect has memorised a part without a single slip.

clue.text: Sound continuously from rarer bee vet treated

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed or worked on, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual bee being cared for by a vet keeps buzzing.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise that reverberates echoes and resounds repeatedly.

clue.text: Number furious to see traveller

parts.note: furious means mad, as in angry

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged by the number of travellers they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place without a fixed home, so is a wanderer or traveller.

clue.text: Bad poetry on poster, perhaps

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a poster is one example of an ad or advertisement
verse is another word for poetry

explanation.surface: Poor-quality lines of poetry printed on a poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like it describes the poetry, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are unfavourable or harmful ones, so the word means bad.

clue.text: Some cube numbers can be dull

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arithmetic with cubed numbers can be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'can be dull' as the definition, but the verb is just 'dull' (to deaden); 'can be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To deaden feeling, making it numb or less sharp, is to dull it.

clue.text: Nicely stranded in base invaded by sudden attack

indicators.note: a place invaded by something has it inside it

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a river bed
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck at a base overrun by a surprise attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranded' looks like marooned but means made of strands.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair that is braided has had its strands neatly woven together.

clue.text: Tastelessly loud supporter's disheartened, say

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment, and the 's adds S

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart or middle letter is removed from the word say

explanation.surface: A fan's spirits are dashed, and they are told so, perhaps by someone vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle out of SAY, leaving SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy describes something showy and loud in a vulgar, brazen way.

clue.text: Cross that is large breed of dog

parts.note: to span a river is to cross it
i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An angry dog of a big breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a type of dog with long drooping ears, such as the cocker.

clue.text: Cat good catching mice and weasel finally

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: fine means good

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the words mice and weasel

explanation.surface: A capable cat catches mice and, at last, a weasel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline means of or like a cat, and as a noun names a member of the cat family.

clue.text: Missionary has job cutting beer

indicators.note: one word cutting another goes into the middle of it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A missionary has taken work that reduces beer drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is one sent out to spread a faith, such as the early Christian missionaries.

clue.text: Cruel person's beheaded river mammal

indicators.note: beheaded removes the head, the first letter of the word

parts.note: a rotter is a cruel or unpleasant person; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A cruel man has decapitated a river creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating mammal living along rivers.

clue.text: Precise English — Times to take action

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
to act is to take action

explanation.surface: An English newspaper, The Times, is urged to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and precise both mean accurate in every detail.

clue.text: Causing anxiety decades before EU's beginning

indicators.note: before places this piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: a decade is a group of ten, so decades are tens

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of EU's

explanation.surface: Years of worry before the European Union came into being.
explanation.definitionFit: A tense situation is a strained, nerve-racking one that makes people anxious.

clue.text: Drive to discourage people on motorway

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI with the figure one as I
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A campaign to stop people driving on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway from London to Leeds; the figure 1 stands in as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive in the sense of determination is the resolve and energy to keep going.

clue.text: Missing light vessel to east of delta

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so this piece goes after the other

parts.note: Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ark is a boat or vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A ship lacking a light sits east of a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to east of' places ARK after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Without illumination a place is dark, lacking any brightness.

clue.text: Military call always recalled unwell European

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A sick European is always being summoned again.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal sounded to wake soldiers in the morning.
